# `silk/url/url`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Parse, serialize, and change URLs as the WHATWG URL Standard specifies, the way web browsers
and JavaScript's `URL` do.

## When to use
Use [`Url`](#Url) for URLs that come from the web or from people: links, `fetch` targets, and
request URLs. It accepts what browsers accept and normalizes it the same way. For strict RFC
3986 URIs, use `silk.uri.uri`.

## Details
A [`Url`](#Url) holds one ASCII string, its serialization, and the positions of its components, so
reading a component does not allocate. [`Url.parse`](#Url.impl.parse) resolves a relative input against a base.
The setters, such as [`Url.setPathname`](#Url.impl.setPathname), follow the URL Standard's API setters: an input that
cannot change the component leaves the URL as it is. Non-ASCII text is percent-encoded as UTF-8
and domains are converted with UTS #46, so the serialization is always ASCII.

## Errors
- `OutOfMemoryError` from every function that allocates.

## Examples
### Parse a URL and read its parts
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.url.url { Url }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let parsed = run Url.parse("HTTPS://Example.COM:443/a/./b/../c?x=1#top", Option<&Url>.none())
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let url = match parsed {
    Option<Url>.Some { value } => value
    Option<Url>.None => { return 1 }
  }
  if Url.href(&url) != "https://example.com/a/c?x=1#top" || Url.pathname(&url) != "/a/c" {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `Url` with `import silk.url.url { Url }`.

<a id="Url"></a>

## `Url`

```silk
pub struct Url
```

A URL as the WHATWG URL Standard defines it: its serialization and the positions of its
components.

### Details
The serialization is `scheme:`, then `//`, user information, the host, and the port when the URL
has a host, then the path, `?` and the query, and `#` and the fragment. A `Url` owns it. The
getters return views of it, with the same text as the getters of JavaScript's `URL`.

### Gotchas
A URL with an opaque path, such as `mailto:a@example.com`, has a path that is one string, not
segments, and [`Url.setPathname`](#Url.impl.setPathname) does not change it.

<a id="Url.impl.parse"></a>

### Associated function `parse`

```silk
pub effect fn parse(input: string, base: Option<&Url>) -> Option<Url>
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Parses `input` as a URL, relative to `base` when it is given. Returns `None` if `input` is
not a valid URL.

#### Details
It is the URL Standard's basic URL parser with UTF-8 encoding. Leading and trailing C0 controls
and spaces are removed, and so are all tabs and newlines. `input` can be relative only when
`base` is given.

#### Errors
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` fails.

<a id="Url.impl.appendOrigin"></a>

### Method `appendOrigin`

```silk
pub effect fn appendOrigin(self: &Self, output: &mut String) -> ()
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Appends the serialization of the URL's origin to `output`, as JavaScript's `URL.origin` does.

#### Details
The origin of an `http`, `https`, `ws`, `wss`, or `ftp` URL is its scheme, host, and port:
`https://example.com:8443`. A `blob` URL has the origin of the URL in its path when that URL is
`http` or `https`. Every other URL has an opaque origin, serialized as `null`.

#### Errors
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` fails.

    ! OutOfMemoryError

<a id="Url.impl.setProtocol"></a>

### Method `setProtocol`

```silk
pub effect fn setProtocol(self: &mut Self, input: string) -> ()
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Sets the scheme from `input` up to its first `:`, as JavaScript's `protocol` setter does.

#### Details
A special scheme cannot change to a scheme that is not special or the reverse, a URL with
credentials or a port cannot become a `file` URL, and a `file` URL with an empty host keeps
its scheme. A port that is the new scheme's default is removed.

#### Errors
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` fails.

<a id="Url.impl.setPort"></a>

### Method `setPort`

```silk
pub effect fn setPort(self: &mut Self, input: string) -> ()
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Sets the port from the digits at the start of `input`, as JavaScript's `port` setter does.

#### Details
An empty `input` removes the port. A port that is the scheme's default is removed. Text that
does not start with a digit, or a value above 65535, leaves the URL as it is. A URL with no
host, an empty host, or the `file` scheme keeps its port.

#### Errors
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` fails.
